blocks.markdown: Definitions cited by the syllabus: Section 3(f)–(l)

**Information and Communications System (Sec. 3(f)).** A system for generating, sending, receiving, storing or otherwise processing electronic data messages or documents — including the computer system or similar device recording, transmitting or storing data, and any related procedure. It covers both the system and the procedures used.

**Personal Information (Sec. 3(g)).** Any information, in material form or not, from which an individual's identity is apparent or can reasonably and directly be ascertained by the holder — or which, together with other information, would directly and certainly identify the individual. Data may identify alone or in combination, and need not be tangible.

**Personal Information Controller (Sec. 3(h)).** A person or organization controlling the collection, holding, processing or use of personal information, including one who instructs another to do so on his behalf. Excluded: (1) one who merely performs such functions as instructed by another, and (2) an individual acting in connection with personal, family or household affairs.

**Personal Information Processor (Sec. 3(i)).** A qualified natural or juridical person to whom a PIC outsources the processing of a data subject's personal data. The PIP processes on the PIC's behalf.

**Processing (Sec. 3(j)).** Any operation or set of operations on personal information, including collection, recording, organization, storage, updating or modification, retrieval, consultation, use, consolidation, blocking, erasure or destruction. It covers nearly every data lifecycle operation, not only collection and disclosure.

**Privileged Information (Sec. 3(k)).** Any data constituting privileged communication under the Rules of Court and other pertinent laws. Privilege is determined by evidence rules and other laws; DPA protection does not itself create privilege.

**Sensitive Personal Information (Sec. 3(l)).** Personal information (1) about race, ethnic origin, marital status, age, color, or religious, philosophical or political affiliations; (2) about health, education, genetic or sexual life, or proceedings for an offense committed or allegedly committed, their disposal, or the court's sentence; (3) issued by government agencies peculiar to an individual (e.g. SSS numbers, health records, licenses or their denial/suspension/revocation, tax returns); or (4) established by executive order or statute to be kept classified. Section 13 imposes a stricter rule on processing it.

blocks.markdown: Section 4 is broad: it covers all types of personal information and any natural or juridical person involved in processing, including controllers and processors not found or established in the Philippines who use equipment located here or maintain an office, branch or agency here, subject to Section 5. It does not apply to: (a) specified government-officer/employee position information; (b) government contract-service information; (c) discretionary financial-benefit information such as licenses or permits; (d) processing for journalistic, artistic, literary or research purposes; (e) information necessary for public-authority functions, including the central monetary authority and law-enforcement/regulatory agencies; (f) bank/financial-institution information needed for CISA (RA 9510), AMLA (RA 9160) and other applicable laws; and (g) personal information of foreign-jurisdiction residents collected under foreign law and processed here. Match the exact information and processing to the exclusion; do not assume an entire organization is exempt.

Section 5 preserves RA 53 protection for publishers, editors and duly accredited reporters of general-circulation publications against being compelled to reveal a confidentially related news source. It is not a blanket exemption for all media-held information.

A foreign entity or offshore storage does not end the inquiry. Section 6 applies the Act to acts done or practices engaged in outside the Philippines where: (a) the processing relates to a Philippine citizen or resident; (b) the entity has a Philippine link — processing here, or processing abroad about citizens/residents with links such as a contract entered here, central management and control here, or a branch/agency/office/subsidiary here whose parent or affiliate accesses the data; and (c) the entity has other Philippine links such as carrying on business here or collecting/holding the data through a Philippine entity. Test both the data-subject connection and the Philippine links.
